Modal B200 quick smoke after Python CuTe/CUTLASS migration. BenchmarkConfig uses warmup_runs=1, iterations=3, num_trials=1. Quick helper caps workloads at 3. Dispatch thresholds: total_seq_len<=1024 and num_seqs<=8 => small path, otherwise large. Full workload run skipped per user direction.

Modal B200 full workload run after Python CuTe/CUTLASS migration. BenchmarkConfig uses warmup_runs=1, iterations=3, num_trials=1. All 100 workloads passed. Dispatch thresholds: total_seq_len<=1024 and num_seqs<=8 => small path, otherwise large.
CUDA V-parallel sequential kernel with fused gates (shared memory state). All 100 passed. Short (<0.5ms): 51, long (>=5ms): 27.
Register-cached V-parallel CUDA kernel. 3x faster than shared-mem version. Still 3.2x slower than CuTe-DSL for long sequences.
Optimized CuTe-DSL wrapper: removed validation, GPU-side cu_seqlens metadata (no full CPU sync), streamlined gate computation. Beats previous 0.3426ms by 2.6%. Only 2 workloads >1ms.
Hybrid dispatch: NVRTC sequential (fused gates) for T<=512, fused gate + CuTe-DSL for T>512. THRESHOLD=512.
Tuned THRESHOLD=128, precomputed max_s_q, fmaf intrinsics. Sweep: 64=0.284, 128=0.284, 256=0.294, 512=0.313, 1024=0.390. 17% improvement over original 0.343ms. 17 workloads >0.5ms.
Step1 refactor: remove prepare_g_beta + validate_inputs from prefill_contract.py
Step2 refactor: remove can_implement + _validate_task6_wrapper_inputs + import warnings + VALID_PATH_NAMES from gdn.py
Step3 refactor: inline _get_dtype_name, _make_compiled_artifact_key, make_cache_key; simplify _get_compiled_gdn_prefill_kernel to path_name only
Step4 refactor: inline choose_path into main.py/gdn.py, delete dispatch.py

Double-buffered async-style k/q + scalar prefetch + 1-sync-per-token in sequential_kernel.cu. Result: 0.296ms vs previous 0.282ms — slight regression (~4%). Only affects T<=128 workloads (already fast); added complexity hurt short sequences. 18 workloads >0.5ms (CuTe-DSL path unchanged). REVERTING.

Python dispatch optimization: cached CUstream, pre-created ctypes constants, get_cu_seqlens_metadata for cached max_s_q (avoids GPU sync), pre-allocated gate_log/beta tensors per (T,device), pre-computed _DEFAULT_SCALE. Result: 0.282ms→0.2732ms (-3.1%). 17 workloads >0.5ms.

Added caching in gdn.py chunk_gated_delta_rule: _cached_stream, _output_cache (keyed by shape+dtype+device), _state_cache. Avoids torch.empty per call on repeat shapes (warmup + 3 timed iterations per workload → 75% cache hit rate). Result: 0.2723→0.2662ms (-2.2%). Min latency 0.070→0.069ms. 17 workloads >0.5ms.

Added sequential-path tensor caches in main.py (_seq_output_cache, _seq_state_cache). Helps T<=128 workloads avoid torch.empty per call. Result: 0.2662→0.2639ms (-0.9%). Min latency 0.069→0.065ms. Cumulative vs 0.282 baseline: -6.4%.

Pre-compute 4D unsqueezed views for gate_log/beta in _get_gate_tensors cache, avoid .unsqueeze(0) per call. Result: 0.2639→0.2629ms (-0.4%, noise level). Cumulative vs 0.282 baseline: -6.8%. Further Python optimizations show diminishing returns; bottleneck is now the CuTe-DSL GPU kernel time for the 17 slow workloads (>0.5ms each).

Fast-launch path: pre-allocated ctypes arg arrays (_SeqArgs, _GateArgs) + direct drv.cuLaunchKernel call, bypassing generic launch() helper. Eliminates per-call ctypes object creation and arg-loop overhead. Result: 0.2629→0.2365ms (-10.0%). Min latency 0.064→0.041ms (-36%). 17 workloads >0.5ms (CuTe-DSL path unchanged). Cumulative vs 0.282 baseline: -16.1%.

Add get_gdn_bundle fast-path in gdn.py: caches (compiled_gdn, output, output_state, problem_size, scale) by (problem_size, scale, path_name). main.py now calls compiled_gdn directly without chunk_gated_delta_rule wrapper. Saves function call + redundant num_seqs/sum_s_q/max_s_q computation per iteration. Result: 0.2365→0.2347ms (-0.8%). Cumulative vs 0.282: -16.8%.

Skip .unsqueeze(0) on q/k/v at call site. data_ptr() is identical for 3D and unsqueezed 4D views; compilation already used 4D iterators. get_gdn_bundle now accepts 3D or 4D and handles internally. Result: 0.2347→0.2277ms (-3.0%). Min 0.040→0.039ms. Cumulative vs 0.282: -19.3%.

Cache squeezed 3D view of output in bundle, return it instead of calling .squeeze(0) per call. Result: 0.2277→0.2287ms (noise level). The .squeeze(0) overhead was already negligible. Keeping the change since it's semantically cleaner.

Cache data_ptr() for stable cached tensors (gate_log, beta, output, output_state) in _get_gate_tensors and get_gdn_bundle. Avoids .data_ptr() calls for these in hot path — 4 fewer Python method calls per long-path call. Result: ~0.227ms stable across runs. Cumulative vs 0.282 baseline: -19.7%.

Threshold re-tuning with optimized Python dispatch. Sweep: T=16→0.2265, T=32→0.225(avg), T=64→0.223(avg, best), T=128→0.2265. With fast-launch path reducing CuTe-DSL per-call overhead, the crossover shifted from 128 down to 64. Cumulative vs 0.282 baseline: -21.0%.

Attempted CUDA stream-capture to graph for the long path (gate + CuTe-DSL). cuStreamBeginCapture failed silently for 59/60 shapes — TVM FFI's compiled_gdn does host-side work incompatible with stream capture. No net improvement (0.2235 ~= 0.2229 baseline). REVERTED.

Enabled persistent scheduling in CuTe-DSL kernel (removed artificial ValueError, set is_persistent=True in GDN() ctor and _compute_grid). Grid reduces from (1,8,num_seqs) to (min(SM_count, num_tiles), 1, 1), improving scheduling for multi-seq workloads. Barrier infrastructure (epi_load_sync_bar_id) was already in place. Result: 0.2229→0.2175ms (-2.4%). All 100 pass. Max 0.942→0.919ms. Cumulative vs 0.282 baseline: -22.9%.

Threshold re-sweep with persistent mode: T=32→0.2191, T=64→0.2175, T=128→0.207/0.223/0.223 (high variance), T=256→0.2318. T=64 and T=128 tied at ~0.218-0.223ms. Best observed: T=128 first run at 0.2069ms (possibly lucky). Setting THRESHOLD=128 as cleaner default.

Final stable state: persistent scheduling + THRESHOLD=64. Multiple runs show mean ~0.222-0.224ms (variance ±0.003ms). First persistent run showed 0.2175 (outlier, possibly warm GPU thermals). Cumulative vs 0.282 baseline: -21.0%. 0.2ms target not reached in stable runs.

Attempt: max_s_q-based dispatch with SEQ_THRESHOLD=128. Routes workloads where max_s_q<=128 to sequential path. Regressed (0.2228->0.2314, +3.9%). Likely single-seq T=65-128 workloads are slower on sequential than CuTe-DSL. REVERTED.
Attempt: max_s_q-based dispatch with SEQ_THRESHOLD=64 (check max_s_q for T>64). Within noise (0.2228->0.2211). Few multi-seq workloads with max_s_q<=64 but T>64 exist in the benchmark. REVERTED.

Attempt: targeted multi-seq dispatch (max_s_q<=128 only when num_seqs>1). Avoids moving single-seq T=65-128 to slow sequential. Still within noise (0.2234 ~ 0.2228 baseline). Workload distribution lacks multi-seq batches in the sweet spot. REVERTED.

Exploration iteration 1 (Model B / FLA Triton adaptation). REGRESSION: 0.2228->0.6593 (+196%). FLA Triton kernel is ~3x slower than vendored CuTe-DSL on B200 for this workload distribution. Long-tail (>0.5ms) grew from 17 workloads to 72. Root cause: Triton's Blackwell tcgen05 codegen underperforms CuTe DSL for chunked linear attention; FLA also uses chunk_size=64 (2x more chunks) and does not exploit GVA (we had to duplicate q/k heads 4->8). Hypothesis FALSIFIED per §2.7. Feature flag reverted to USE_FLA=0 default. FLA path kept as dead code for future reference.

L1 broadcast optimization: removed shared memory + __syncthreads in sequential kernel, all threads read k/q directly from global via __ldg() (L1 cache broadcast). Result: 0.2228->0.2098ms (-5.8%). 45 workloads <0.1ms (was ~40), 17 workloads >0.5ms (unchanged, CuTe-DSL path). Min latency 0.041ms.
Threshold sweep with L1-broadcast kernel: T=64→0.2098/0.2090 (stable), T=72→0.2130, T=96→0.2369, T=128→0.2280. Vectorized uint4 loads→0.2181. All regressions. T=64 remains optimal. REVERTED to T=64.

Attempt: 4-way dot product accumulation in sequential kernel (kS and out_val). Split 128-long serial FMA chain into 4 independent chains of 32. Expected 2-4% gain from better Blackwell FMA pipeline utilization. Result: REGRESSION 0.2098->0.2256 (+7.5%). Min latency 0.041->0.043ms. Hypothesis falsified: either NVCC was already doing this transform (compiler already broke chain via instruction scheduling) or Blackwell FMA latency is shorter than assumed (not 4 cycles), so the dependency chain was not the bottleneck. Increased register pressure from 4 live k values + 4 accumulators likely caused measurable slowdown. REVERTED.

Single-seq max_s_q shortcut: when num_seqs==1, skip get_cu_seqlens_metadata and use max_s_q=T (exactly correct, no GPU sync). Avoids 5-10us GPU->CPU sync for ~half the CuTe-DSL workloads. Result: 0.2098->0.2064 (-1.6%). 100/100 pass, no RUNTIME_ERRORs. Min latency 0.041->0.039. Cumulative vs 0.282 baseline: -26.8%.

Cache max_s_q by (T, num_seqs) to bypass get_cu_seqlens_metadata sync. Result: mean=0.1917ms on 98 workloads BUT 2 workloads (5835a2bc, cd979341) got RUNTIME_ERROR (GPU Xid 13 Illegal Instruction Parameter + context corruption). Root cause: (T, num_seqs) collisions - two different workloads share (T, num_seqs) but have different actual max_s_q. Cached wrong value -> kernel OOB/wrong tile count -> GPU crash. REVERTED to safe single-seq-only variant.

FAILED: using max_s_q=T for all workloads (eliminate sync entirely). Safe (overestimate) but CuTe-DSL very sensitive to max_s_q: empty-tile overhead dominates. Result: 0.2064->0.4076 (+97%). Max latency 0.86->2.80ms. REVERTED.
FAILED: replace get_cu_seqlens_metadata with int((cu_seqlens[1:]-cu_seqlens[:-1]).max()). Two GPU kernel launches (subtract+max) add ~10us overhead per call. Result: 0.2064->0.2313 (+12%). REVERTED.

Replace get_cu_seqlens_metadata with inline cu_seqlens.tolist() + Python max for multi-seq workloads. Skips weakref/dict bookkeeping that always misses due to clone-per-iteration. Results: 2 runs 0.2057 + 0.2051 = avg 0.2054ms (-0.5% vs 0.2064). 100/100 pass. 47-48 workloads <0.1ms, 16 >0.5ms.

NCU-style profiling on Modal B200 (torch.profiler + CUDA events) for 8 representative workloads. Confirmed overhead breakdown: sequential=15us constant, CuTe-DSL=50us (TVM FFI 15-20us, gate launch 5us, Python dispatch 15-20us, multi-seq D2H 3-5us). Medium CuTe-DSL workloads (T=100-1000) have overhead=50-70% of total. Long workloads (>0.5ms) are kernel-compute-dominated. See optimization_log.md for full table. No code change this iteration; committed scripts/profile_modal.py as infrastructure.

NCU-guided: __launch_bounds__(128,1) -> (128,2). NCU showed Block Limit Registers=2 so register budget allowed 2 blocks/SM, but grid only has 8 blocks for single-seq so packing 2/SM halves SMs used. Result: 0.2054->0.2192 (+6.7%, partly GPU noise). Revert run measured 0.2177 suggesting most is noise. REVERTED. Real bottleneck: insufficient grid parallelism, not per-SM occupancy.
